Updates Astro from 7.0.4 to 7.0.7, Lucide Astro from 1.22.0 to 1.24.0, Simple Icons from 16.24.1 to 16.25.0, refreshes the Bun lockfile, and revises the existing dependency changelog entry.

target.title: chore(deps): refresh site dependencies
target.body:
## Summary

- update Astro from 7.0.4 to 7.0.7
- update Lucide Astro from 1.22.0 to 1.24.0
- update Simple Icons from 16.24.1 to 16.25.0
- refresh the Bun lockfile and existing dependency changelog entry

## Upstream review

- [Astro 7.0.7](https://github.com/withastro/astro/releases/tag/astro%407.0.7) is a patch release with build, CSS, dev-server, and preload-marker fixes.
- Lucide Astro 1.24.0 retains explicit Astro 7 peer compatibility.
- [Simple Icons 16.25.0](https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons/releases/tag/16.25.0) adds one icon.
- Registry integrity values match the committed Bun lockfile.

## Exact-head proof

Commit: `7e321d0e47187bc583b9a22a05680f898cf5ff02`

- tree is byte-for-byte identical to the privately proven original candidate `04612ad273a8a7aec0110847f1c4fccc381b6d7a`
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: clean, no lockfile changes
- `bun outdated`: no outdated direct dependencies
- `bun audit`: no vulnerabilities found
- `bun test`: 39 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run test:built-assets`: passed
- `bun run build`: 31 pages built; repeated cleanly
- built-browser proof: the exact Astro 7.0.7 preview was loaded through the existing Chrome profile using Peekaboo; navigation, CTAs, stats, Lucide UI icons, and branded integration icons rendered correctly
- autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.96
- Public Model Identifier Gate: PASS. The exact diff, lockfile, generated build, proof logs, and this PR text add no model identifiers or model-bearing artifacts.

## Vercel isolation

Vercel rejects preview creation before a build begins. Three distinct exact heads were tested: the full update, the update with Astro retained, and Simple Icons alone. All failed instantly with no preview URL, so the failure does not track any package or lockfile graph.

The invariant is the Git commit author. Vercel documents that Pro-team deployments require the commit author's GitHub login to be connected to a Vercel account with project-team access: [Why aren't commits triggering deployments on Vercel?](https://vercel.com/kb/guide/why-aren-t-commits-triggering-deployments-on-vercel).

Repository CI, local production builds, and browser proof are green. Merge remains blocked until the Vercel author-access requirement is resolved and both exact-head previews pass.

Risk: low in the dependency diff; current merge risk is the unresolved external preview-authorization gate.
